parts:
Have installed rapache on OSX (big thanks to Karsten for the
tutorial!).
www.myhost.com/RApacheInfo pops up successfully.

However, despite reading the manual & READMEs, I can't run the test
scripts.

www.myhost.com/rapache-1.1.9/test/ leads to a page of demos like
Hello World, but Hello World produces: Oops! This link appears to be
broken.
Apache error logs say the file does not exist:

File does not exist: /Library/WebServer/Documents/test, referer:
http://mysite.com/rapache-1.1.9/test/

but it's here:
/library/webserver/documents/rapache-1.1.9/test/helloworld.r

"Brew: novice application" leads to a literal display, rather than
execution, of the code.

Could someone suggest an intelligent directory structure to minimize
path errors?

Right now I have:
/docroot/R-2.11.1
/docroot/brew
/docroot/rapache-1.1.9
/docroot/rscripts

Does this make sense or should I run all r scripts under brew? or
what? and how does this affect the Location and Directory settings
suggested for httpd.conf ?

Also, in the README for rapache, does
"# This url will run the file /path/to/r/script.R"

mean r = path to rapache? or path to R?

Do I have to create a Location directive in httpd.conf for every
script I use?

confused

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: installed but stalled (OSX)
parts:
Okay, to get the brew files working place this in your apache config:

<Directory /Library/WebServer/Documents/brew>
SetHandler r-script
RHandler brew::brew
</Directory>

Two things:

1. Be sure brew is installed in R
2. Be sure that the files under /Library/WebServer/Documents/brew are
readable by the web server user id.

Report back when you get a change, and then we'll move on to using <Location>.

Jeff
